bullets: How one condition of demand works: incomes rise, the whole demand curve shifts, a shortage opens, and competition bids the price up to a new equilibrium
slides.heading: Demand and supply: an income rise bids the price up
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow one market as incomes rise - and check whether buyers slide along a curve or the curve itself moves.

bullets: Describe the starting equilibrium where supply and demand cross at price P1 and quantity Q1
Explain why a rise in income shifts the whole demand curve right, and trace the shortage and price rise that follow
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to say why the curve shifts, not slides.

bullets: After incomes rise, buyers want a bigger quantity - so it looks as if they simply moved along the same demand curve
But they want more at every price, even at the old price - so what really changed?
slides.heading: Bigger quantity - slide or shift?
slides.notes: Ask the class: did buyers slide along the curve, or did the curve move? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because scene 2 names the real change.

bullets: Demand is the quantity buyers want at each price; supply is the quantity firms offer at each price
Income is a condition of demand: when it changes for a normal good, the whole demand curve shifts
Only a change in the good's own price causes a movement along a curve
slides.heading: A condition change shifts the whole curve
slides.notes: Stress the deciding distinction: a price change moves along a curve, a condition change shifts the whole curve. Supply does not move in this lesson.

bullets: Supply and demand cross at the equilibrium E1
At price P1 the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded, Q1
slides.heading: The market starts in equilibrium
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the crossing: follow the market marker as it climbs the supply curve and settles where the two curves meet.

bullets: Consumer income rises, and for a normal good buyers want more at every price
The whole demand curve shifts right from D1 to D2; supply does not move
slides.heading: Incomes rise and demand shifts right
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and trace the shift: the whole curve moves right - this is not a movement along the curve.

bullets: At the old price P1, buyers on the new demand curve want Qd but firms still supply only Qs
The gap between Qd and Qs is a shortage
slides.heading: A shortage opens at the old price
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and stretch the gap: at P1 quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, so unsatisfied buyers compete for the good.

bullets: Competing buyers bid the price up along the unchanged supply curve
The market settles at the new equilibrium E2 - price P2, quantity Q2 - where the new demand curve crosses supply
slides.heading: Competition bids the price up to a new equilibrium
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and follow the marker climbing supply in steps until the shortage closes at E2.

bullets: If buyers only slid along the same demand curve, demand at the old price P1 would stay at Q1
But at P1 buyers now want Qd, more than Q1 - so the whole curve must have shifted, opening the shortage that bids the price up
slides.heading: Worked example: testing the slide claim in this market
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, state the slide claim. Step 2, at the unchanged price P1 the quantity demanded has risen from Q1 to Qd, which a slide along the same curve cannot explain. Step 3, a shift of demand - followed by the shortage and the price rise along supply - is the explanation that fits.

bullets: In pairs: put equilibrium, the demand shift, the shortage and the new equilibrium into one causal chain
Then swap and check: does the chain start with the income rise and end at P2 and Q2?
slides.heading: Your turn: explain the chain
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for the whole curve shifting named as the driver, then take two pairs answers.

bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says a rise in income only moves buyers along the same demand curve
Name the shift of the whole demand curve as the real change to earn full credit
slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers say the curve itself shifts - only a price change moves along it.
